duties.duty: The full named comparison across every allocated mean-power regime and preserved source-specific variant remains unassessed; the read L1/L2 and stated p>=1 norm arguments are positive evidence, not proof of absence or of whole-regime fulfillment.
duties.gap: The new comparison chapter covers the three ranges 0<p<1, p=1, 1<p<infinity (power/metric facts, L^p inside L^q, a.s./probability/distribution implications, the general-p Vitali theorem, five countermodels and the 12-pair failure count, with Durrett Lemma 2.2.2, Thms 2.3.2-2.3.4, Exs 2.3.11-2.3.12, 3.2.12 and Thms 4.6.2-4.6.3 checked in the held PDF). But item (6) of thm:p15-w02b-p15-013-comparison (parts lines 215-220) asserts an "if and only if": X_n->X in probability and in L^p iff X_n in L^p for every n and (|X_n|^p) is uniformly integrable. The annex proof (annex lines 198-199) only cites thm:p15-w02b-p15-013-vitali, whose hypotheses already assume X_n in L^p (parts line 231); the necessity of X_n in L^p and of uniform integrability is never argued, and it fails under the chapter's own definition (parts lines 77-78, 85-88): X_n=X=Y with E|Y|^p=infinity converges in L^p (E|X_n-X|^p=0) and in probability, yet X_n is not in L^p and |X_n|^p is not uniformly integrable. The named probability-to-mean comparison is therefore not fully established as stated; it needs the hypothesis X_n in L^p (or X in L^p) added, or the equivalence restated as in the Vitali theorem.
